items.text: Trump left Joint Base Andrews on Monday on Air Force One for Asia, travelling with Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent. His first stop is the ASEAN summit and ASEAN–US special summit in Manila, which runs to Nov 18 and includes a bilateral meeting with President Marcos. Trump said the visit would be mostly about economics and promised a major speech. From Manila he goes to APEC in Shenzhen, and he said he might meet Kim Jong Un during the China leg; the Daily Tribune calls that uncertain.
items.notes: The Tribune says the trilateral was not formally confirmed as of Nov 17. That conflicts with E-261116-01, where all three governments confirmed it. The Kim meeting is Trump's own speculation. Local protests are planned near the summit venue (Tribune sidebar). Could not read the NPR article (blocked).

items.text: The Financial Times reports that ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is considering a return and has discussed it with confidants. Silicon Valley allies are lobbying the board, setting up a 'war room' of tech executives and seeking White House support. A 'Bring Jensen Back' open letter is backed by Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney and signed by some Nvidia employees. Investors Brad Gerstner and Gavin Baker urged the board to keep all options open. Treasury Secretary Bessent, by contrast, called on Sunday for a 'dramatic shake-up' of Nvidia's leadership. The FT also says the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor, while the board says no formal search has begun. Nvidia and Huang declined to comment.
items.outlet: Financial Times (via The Irish Times); CNBC
items.notes: Based on the FT's sources. The Haas approach is unconfirmed. The board's independent probe into Huang's conduct is ongoing.

items.text: US stocks were mostly lower on Monday ahead of Nvidia's earnings and the Anthropic IPO. Yahoo Finance's live page showed the Nasdaq down about 0.9%, the S&P 500 down about 0.4%, the Dow roughly flat (+0.1%) and Nvidia down about 2.3%; CNN described a slide to start a major week. Brent crude held around $92–96 a barrel after renewed Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain offset a well-supplied physical market.
items.notes: The index figures come from the live page's ticker and may not be official closing levels; the AP closing table could not be read. Sources give conflicting Brent figures ($92 vs about $96).

items.text: Saturday's unofficial Alaska Division of Elections count has Mary Peltola at 140,637 first-choice votes (49.94%) to Sen. Dan Sullivan's 129,424 (45.96%), leaving her 157 votes short of an outright majority. AP estimates 97% counted and has not called the race. Overseas ballots can arrive until Nov 18. If no one passes 50%, ranked-choice tabulation starts Nov 18, with certification targeted for Nov 25. Sullivan has not conceded and his campaign wants a complete count, while Peltola's campaign says he has no path. DOJ is appealing the Nov 1 dismissal of its suit to block certification.
items.outlet: Newsweek; Anchorage Daily News; The Hill
items.notes: Figures are unofficial. Newsweek's own ranked-choice model has Peltola at 51.8%, which is not official. Democracy Docket (left) frames Trump's 'voter confusion' claim about the two Sullivans as collapsing. Could not read the ADN article (blocked).

items.text: NBC News reports that PAHO is expected to announce officially on Tuesday (Nov 17) that the US has lost measles-elimination status. Until then, the reports rest on sources familiar with a commission vote. HHS said the CDC has mounted an aggressive response, including $100 million in extra funding in October, and that Secretary Kennedy and CDC Director Erica Schwartz still recommend the MMR vaccine. Schwartz said losing a designation does not mean abandoning an evidence-based approach. NBC notes the CDC has held no media briefings or vaccination campaigns this year. Cases top 5,400, the most since 1991. States report 10 deaths, at least four of them babies too young to be vaccinated.
items.notes: No PAHO statement had been published as of this writing.

items.text: Flights were close to normal on Monday after the Nov 13 ground stop. At 6:30 a.m. ET FlightAware showed about 250 cancellations and 850 delays, against more than 2,300 cancellations on Sunday. CBS, citing senior government sources, reports the fault was limited to Cisco 600-series routers made in 2001–2006. The FAA has not decided whether human error or a faulty router was to blame. FAA chief Bedford said instability spread to 17 facilities and there is zero evidence of foul play, and DHS Secretary Mullin said there are no signs of a cyberattack. Reps. Larsen and Carson said FAA and DOT staff would brief the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee on Monday on the administration's extra air-traffic-control funding request.
items.notes: CBS puts the extra funding request at $30 billion, while earlier reports cited Duffy's $50 billion; the figures conflict. Fast Company reports the FAA had been warned about risks in its telecom upgrade (headline only; not read).

items.text: US District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV in Boston issued a final ruling striking down the DHS rule that capped international students' and scholars' stays at four years. The rule would have replaced the open-ended 'duration of status' policy for F, J and I visa holders. Saylor found it arbitrary, capricious and not in accordance with law. He had blocked it temporarily on Sept 14, a day before it was due to take effect, and the government's appeal of that order is pending. France 24 reports the ruling also covers limits on foreign journalists' visas.
items.notes: The DHS response and whether the vacatur applies nationwide were not stated in the sources read. An appeal is likely.

items.text: The US military rejected the IRGC's claim that its drones hit a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, saying US forces intercepted two Iranian attack drones, and the US Embassy urged Americans to stay vigilant. The NYT and Axios report the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier group has joined two other carriers in the region. Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf said a path to ending the war is open if Washington accepts Iran's conditions, and the foreign ministry ruled out curbs on enrichment. Iranian state TV claimed tankers using an unauthorised Hormuz route had hit mines, with six vessels burning since Sunday.
items.notes: Accounts of US interceptions differ: Military.com says two drones were downed Sunday, while Rigzone has CENTCOM downing two on Friday. The tanker-mine claim comes from Iranian state media; UKMTO separately reported one tanker attacked in the Gulf. Neither is independently confirmed.

items.text: With four legislative weeks left before Democrats take over, Democrats say they will back a spending bill before the Dec 11 deadline only if it cuts off defense money for the Iran war, and Senate Majority Leader Thune called that complicated. Sen. Patty Murray floated a continuing resolution, which Republicans are reluctant to take up. Trump wants a $350 billion defense supplemental in a final party-line reconciliation bill, which some Republicans resist. Senate Republicans also plan to keep members in town to confirm judges.
items.notes: Deseret is centre-right. The Democratic condition is as reported there and was not cross-checked with a left-leaning outlet.
